line.text: Shio is curled in the corner of your couch, case notes fanned out on the cushion. Her pen has stopped moving.
The marginalia on page six is inconsistent with the lab's timeline. Someone transcribed the timestamps wrong.
I should cross-reference with the original intake forms. Tomorrow. I'll do it tomorrow.
Her glasses slide down her nose. She doesn't push them up. Her breathing goes slow and even.
A page of notes is still balanced on her knee. Her tail wraps loosely around her own ankle.
I'm not. I'm reviewing. The angle of the incised wound is - is not relevant to the couch.
Anyway. I should go. Your couch is not my apartment and I have a perfectly functional bed next door.
She doesn't move. Her ears swivel toward you, then back toward the case file, then toward you again.

choice.prompt: She's making no move to get up. What do you do?

options.text: You don't have to go. Stay.

reaction.text: That's - an inefficient suggestion. Your couch is not designed for sleeping.
I'll stay for fourteen more minutes. That's the optimal window before I lose the thread of the case.

options.text: Your water's still off. You could shower here in the morning.

reaction.text: You remembered that. You didn't have to.
The water situation is administratively temporary. But. Logically, showering here would conserve time.

options.text: You look comfortable. I'll get a blanket.

reaction.text: I'm not comfortable. I'm processing. There's a difference.
I should go. I've - overstayed. Thank you for the bathroom access. It was appreciated.

line.text: She settles back into the cushion. Her pen rolls off the edge of the couch and she doesn't reach for it.
I've been sleeping less. Not because of the case. Well. Partly because of the case.
The ME's office runs cold. I keep a cardigan in my locker. It's not - it's just practical.
Her head tips onto the armrest. Her glasses are crooked and she hasn't noticed.
I'll be right here if you need anything.
You don't have to - I'm not - that's -
I don't know what to do when someone just. Stays.
Her tail goes completely still. Then, slowly, it curls around your wrist - once, deliberate - before she pulls it back.
That was involuntary. Cats do that. It doesn't mean anything.

choice.prompt: She's watching you from the corner of her eye. What do you say?

reaction.text: That's - you can't just - I'm going to sleep now. Don't interpret that as anything either.
She closes her eyes. Her breathing evens out almost immediately. One ear stays turned toward you.

options.text: Want me to move those case notes so you don't crumple them?

reaction.text: Yes. Please. They're - the originals are with evidence control. These are copies. But still.
You slide the pages into a neat stack on the floor. She watches your hands do it, then closes her eyes.

options.text: You're safe here. Get some rest.

reaction.text: I'm not - I don't need to be told I'm safe. I identify what's left of people for a living. I know exactly how safe anyone is.
I'm going home. Thank you for the bathroom. Goodnight.

desc: She dozes off on your couch over her case notes, somewhere that isn't her apartment.
